Worker-supplied eligibility assertions shall not substitute for this evidence. intelligence.falsifier: A scheduler's eligible:true flag accepted as proof; a fairness violation manufactured from opportunities that never existed; genuine starvation hidden behind false ineligible labels; missing evidence auto-converted to eligible=false (hiding starvation) or eligible=true (false accusation); circular corroboration from one shared untrusted boolean; a saturated scheduler evading fairness by calling every waiting task ineligible; a later taxonomy version retroactively rewriting a historical witness.

human_view.meaning: Counting is easy; proving the count is the work. A scheduler's 'eligible: true' flag is a claim, not evidence — and the law requires six independent facts behind every counted opportunity: the obligation really existed and was still outstanding, LAW actually permitted this exact transition, every dependency was truly ready, the queue and capacity could actually serve it, a real scheduling decision in the right pool actually happened, and all of it refers to one consistent, reconstructable moment. The invariant is a six-way conjunction the verifier computes itself from referenced evidence — never accepting 'enabled_before=true' just because the worker wrote it down. (One nuance that matters: a waiting task doesn't need to have received a worker lease to count as eligible — otherwise starvation could never be detected.) Each opportunity gets a witness packet tying it to an exact scheduler sequence and governing versions, so a cold successor can replay why it counted. The worker's own assertion is kept in the packet for comparison — and then ignored as verdict. Source separation is enforced with teeth: 'authorized=true' from the worker means nothing next to an independently read LAW decision; a hash proves bytes didn't change, not that they describe reality; three systems agreeing on one untrusted boolean is one source, not three. When eligibility changes mid-round — a withdrawal racing a scheduling decision — the verifier uses authoritative commit order, not machine timestamps; a scope split is judged against the taxonomy version that governed that round, and later reclassifications never rewrite history. The verifier answers in three values, not two: proven eligible (count it), proven ineligible (don't, keep the reason), or undetermined — and undetermined is the vital one, because auto-false lets a defective scheduler hide starvation by not recording, while auto-true invents violations. The worked example: with a three-opportunity bound, two proven eligible rounds plus one undetermined round is debt 2 with a gap — not debt 3; only the third proven eligible round at 104 completes the breach, and only if no unobserved service could have filled the gap. The breach rule is universal over all histories consistent with observations — if some breach and some don't, the answer is UNDETERMINED, never PASS, never violation. The scheduling record itself gets eight integrity properties, including the subtle one: contention is not ineligibility — under a capacity-backed fair queue, 'every worker was busy' is exactly when fairness matters, and a saturated scheduler may not define its way out of the obligation. Twelve adversarial tests, crowned by E2 in both directions: false ineligibility hiding three genuinely eligible opportunities must be caught by reconstructing canonical facts; then the reverse — LAW genuinely absent while the worker claims eligible=true — must refuse the false violation.
